payload.title: Standardize the time-bucketed quality ranking as one specified module
payload.description:
**Goal.** The time-bucketed rank-by-quality algorithm is one specified, documented, tested module that every consumer reuses, and it is perfected. Today it lives in `src/papyrus_content/home_page/ordering.py` (`rank_in_buckets`, the shared order: 3-5 stars, then unrated by Cyclotron confidence with unscored last, then 1-2 stars; ties by newest arrival then key), is reused by `src/papyrus_content/projection/standard/story_order.py` for Stories (`listings.bucket`), by the references include (`select="confident|recommended"`, `bucket="day|week"`, docs/home-page.md "Ordering" and "Time buckets"), and by the Worth-watching card. The rules are written in prose in docs/home-page.md; the Stories side and the Worth-watching card have their own copies of parts of it.

**Build.**
- Extract to one module with a small public API (rank, bucket, as-of day) and no consumer-specific logic; Stories, References, the Worth-watching card, lists and the roundup selection call it. Remove duplicate copies (no shims).
- One standalone doc page of the algorithm: inputs, rolling UTC windows, bucket date (acceptedAt, then arrivedAt, then oldest), order inside a bucket, tie rules, what a rating never changes, what time does.
- Gherkin for each rule; property tests: stable under subsetting, deterministic for a given day, nothing dropped, a rating never changes bucket.
- Perfect it: audit open questions below against the data (distribution of ratings and confidences) and adapt rather than fix constants.

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Time-bucketed quality ranking
  Scenario: Newest bucket first
    Given Stories published in three different weeks
    When ranked with week buckets
    Then every Story of the newest week precedes every Story of the next

  Scenario: Human rating over prediction
    Given a four-star Reference with low Cyclotron confidence and an unrated one with high confidence
    Then the four-star one ranks first inside the bucket

  Scenario: Unscored is not 50 percent
    Given an accepted Reference the Cyclotron never scored
    Then it ranks below every scored unrated Reference

  Scenario: Low ratings sink
    Given a one-star Reference the Cyclotron likes
    Then it ranks below unrated ones

  Scenario: Rating does not move buckets
    When a Reference is rated
    Then its bucket is unchanged

  Scenario: Time moves buckets
    Given a Reference that turns seven days old today
    Then it moves to the older window and follows every newer one

  Scenario: Subsets keep order
    When a section filter is applied to a ranked list
    Then the filtered list is in the same relative order

  Scenario: One implementation
    Then Stories, References, the Worth-watching card and the roundup call the same module
```

**Depends on:** none. Blocks the story-type selection story. Under the home-page epic PPY-1b83d3.
**Related:** PPY-ba2f19 (stars shown), PPY-f24696.

**Open questions for Ryan:** (1) Is a one- or two-star rating a hard sink below unrated, as now? (2) Should bucket width ever be learned from a site's publishing rate instead of day/week?
